You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Awkward Guests: The Walton Case Awkward Guests is a one-of-a-kind deduction game with infinite re-playability. You can recreate Mr. Walton's murder in so many different ways that you won't ever play two similar games! (Mr. Walton will not thank you for doing this.) The game challenges you to use genuine detective abilities to solve each case. To solve a mystery, you have to interrogate the suspects, question the household staff, examine the crime scene, search for clues around the Walton Mansion, and consult the police reports. You will do all of this while exchanging information with your opponents or hiding it from them, so get ready to use all your gumshoe skills! WHO killed Mr. Walton? HOW did the murderer end his life? WHY did the murderer kill him? Was there an ACCOMPLICE? The heart of Awkward Guests is simple: Players have a hand of six cards, and each card has a value (1, 2 or 3 points, according to the amount of information that it provides) and several references (i.e., the subjects of the card information). During a turn, you ask for information about two different references in which you are interested. The rest of the players can offer you cards that contain the requested references, and you can trade for those cards by giving the offering players the same number of points they have offered via cards in your hand. After each round ends, players can try to solve the mystery. If the mystery is not solved, players discard part of their hands and receive three new cards. The player or players who solve the mystery first win. Number of players: 1 - 8 Game duration: 18 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Awkward Guests: The Walton Case and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Exchange Phase (you choose and pay) 1.5 End of the round 1.5.1 Solution Phase (everyone decides at once) 1.5.2 Discard Phase (if continuing) 1.6 If the game deck runs out 1.7 Useful rules for deduction 1.8 What the different card topics usually tell you 2 2-player differences 3 Solo mode Awkward Guests: The Walton Case This is a deduction and information-trading game. All players try to solve the murder on Mr. Walton. The first player to do so correctly, wins the game. Each player has their own investigation sheet (private to them) to keep track of the information they learn during the game. Goal Be the first player to correctly solve the case by identifying: - WHO killed Mr. Walton? - WHY did they kill him (motive)? - HOW did they put an end to his life (weapon)? - Was there an ACCOMPLICE and, if so, WHO and WHY ? (For Beginner / Very Easy / Easy cases there is never an accomplice.) Information in the game Each card has: - an information value (1–3), representing the amount of valuable information, and used to price exchanges; - references (suspects and/or rooms) showing what the info is about; - the case-related information; - how the information can be denoted on the tracking sheet. Round structure The game is played in rounds. In each round, every player takes one turn (anti-clockwise). Each turn has 3 phases: - Inquiry Phase - Offer Phase - Exchange Phase After all players have taken a turn, the round ends with a Solution Phase . If no one has solved the murder in this phase, the game continues with the Discard Phase . Your turn 1. Inquiry Phase (ask for 2 references) On your turn, you must request information about exactly 2 different references: - suspects (the 6 guests), and/or - rooms in the mansion. So you may ask for: 2 suspects, 2 rooms, or 1 suspect and 1 room. Arrows are used to show all players which 2 references have been chosen. 2. [Rating: 1/10] Update :star::nostar::nostar::nostar::nostar:  Deck milling becomes annoying now. I really don't know why it's a thing, but there you go.   -----------------------  Average deduction game. The deck milling of evidence made the game very arbitrary. The choices on who to trade with is either obvious or engages in kingmaking.

[Rating: 1/10] Incómodos Invitados is the spanish version, looks like a good mix for my group, might be good, need to research.

[Rating: 2/10] Presold at price to a fellow gamer in Germany. Waiting for the game to arrive.  The game may be good, but the publishers are bad (terrible, uninformative communication, insisted on having the screen act at the same time as the sheet of paper that requires screening and then misprinted it), so, with so many games around, I don't feel like playing it any longer. So, according to the criteria of BGG this is a solid 2 to me.

[Rating: 2/10] Después de un segundo intento pude probar este juego. El primer intento fue imposible. El diminuto tamaño de la letra en algunos apartados de la hoja de anotaciones junto con la combinación de color sepia, hacía prácticamente imposible jugarlo.  En la segunda intentona, ya condicionada, negativamente, por lo comentado en el punto anterior, el dueño trajo unas lupas para subsanar este fallo de diseño.  Ni con este componente adicional salvó al juego de ser divertido. Fue una hora y cuarto de total aburrimiento, pasas cartas, te dan cartas y te vuelven a venir pistas que ya tenías antes. Mención

[Rating: 2/10] Difficult to set up and time-consuming to put away. Overly complicated Cluedo-like game.

[Rating: 2/10] theme is cool, there is barely any deduction at perfect crime. Just waiting for right cards, there is no game

[Rating: 2/10] Tenía muchas ganas de que me gustara, pero no fue así. Jugamos una partida "muy fácil" y fue compleja y extremadamente larga. Todavía no entiendo que implica la coletilla de un sospechoso "que puede haber visto". Sobrevalorado. El arte western tampoco me entusiasma. Pérdida de dinero

[Rating: 2.5/10] Sorry...the game doesn’t truly play the way it is marketed.  There is deduction in the Character/murderer, some deduction in the weapon (but is usually the most described in the deck and easiest for all to determine) and no deduction in the motive.  Basically, you pass the same cards around for an hour until there is a reshuffle, then you wait for somebody to see the 4 cards that are absolutely needed to determine the answer...I will stick with Sleuth.
